extra.message: User input from params["id"] (the 'id' GET parameter) is concatenated directly into the SQL query string passed to cursor.execute(): "SELECT id, username, name, surname FROM users WHERE id=" + params["id"]. No parameterization or sanitization is applied, allowing UNION-based, boolean-blind and time-blind SQL injection.

The 'v' GET parameter (params["v"]) is reflected unescaped into the HTML response via re.sub substitution into HTML_POSTFIX. An attacker can inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript, resulting in reflected XSS.
Untrusted data from the 'object' GET parameter is deserialized with pickle.loads(params["object"].encode()). pickle deserialization of attacker-controlled data leads to arbitrary code execution.

The 'path' GET parameter is passed to open(os.path.abspath(params["path"])) with no validation, allowing arbitrary local file read (path traversal). When the value contains '://', it is passed to urllib.request.urlopen(), allowing Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) including file:// and internal URLs.
When the 'path' parameter contains '://', urllib.request.urlopen(params["path"]) fetches an attacker-supplied URL with no allowlist, enabling Server-Side Request Forgery against internal services.

The 'domain' GET parameter is concatenated into a shell command: subprocess.run("nslookup " + params["domain"], shell=True, ...). With shell=True and unsanitized input, an attacker can inject arbitrary OS commands (e.g. domain=;id).

The 'xml' GET parameter is parsed with lxml.etree.XMLParser(load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False). Enabling DTD loading, entity resolution, and network access allows XML External Entity (XXE) attacks for local file disclosure and SSRF.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The 'name' GET parameter is interpolated directly into an XPath expression: xpath(".//user[name/text()='%s']" % params["name"]). Unsanitized input allows XPath injection to extract arbitrary data (e.g. passwords) from the XML document.

The 'size' GET parameter is converted via int(params["size"]) and used to build a string of size N*N ("#" * int(size) repeated int(size) times). An attacker-supplied large value causes uncontrolled memory/CPU consumption (Denial of Service).

The 'comment' GET parameter is formatted directly into an INSERT statement via string interpolation: cursor.execute("INSERT INTO comments VALUES(NULL, '%s', '%s')" % (params["comment"], time.ctime())). This allows SQL injection (and stored-XSS in the rendered comments).
Comments stored from the 'comment' parameter (line 50) are later rendered into the HTML table without escaping, resulting in stored/persistent Cross-Site Scripting.

The 'include' parameter loads program text from a local file or remote URL (urllib.request.urlopen when it contains '://') and passes it to exec(program, envs). This allows Remote File Inclusion and arbitrary Python code execution.

The 'include' parameter is fetched via urllib.request.urlopen() when it contains '://', allowing inclusion of a remote attacker-controlled file whose contents are then executed (Remote File Inclusion + SSRF).

cwe: CWE-98: Improper Control of Filename for Include/Require Statement

extra.message: The 'redir' GET parameter is interpolated unescaped into an HTML meta refresh tag: content="0; url=%s" % params["redir"]. An attacker can redirect victims to an arbitrary external site (open redirect) and inject HTML attributes/tags (XSS).

The 'callback' GET parameter is reflected unescaped into the /users.json response as a JSONP wrapper ("%s(" % params["callback"]). The Content-Type can also be coerced to text/html, allowing reflected XSS via the callback value.

The login query concatenates the 'password' parameter directly into SQL: "... AND password='" + params.get("password", "") + "'". The password is not sanitized, allowing authentication bypass via SQL injection (e.g. password=' OR '1' LIKE '1).

On successful login the username (params['username']) is reflected into the HTML response 'Welcome %s' . Although filtered with re.sub(r"[^\w]", ""), the reflection of user-controlled data combined with disabled XSS protection (line 77) constitutes a reflected XSS sink.

On any exception the full traceback (traceback.format_exc()) or subprocess output is returned to the client in the HTTP response, disclosing source code, file paths, and internal state (sensitive information exposure through error messages).

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The 'charset' GET parameter is reflected unsanitized into the Content-Type response header via send_header("Content-Type", ... "; charset=%s" % params.get("charset", "utf8")). Attacker-controlled header values enable HTTP response header injection and can be abused to force charset-based XSS (e.g. UTF-7).

The server explicitly sets the response header 'X-XSS-Protection: 0', disabling the browser's built-in XSS auditor for all responses and increasing the impact of the reflected XSS vulnerabilities in the application.

The HTML_PREFIX inline script reads document.location.hash, extracts the 'lang=' fragment value and writes it into the DOM via document.write(... decodeURIComponent(...)) without sanitization. A crafted URL fragment causes DOM-based Cross-Site Scripting.

USERS_XML contains hardcoded credentials in cleartext (e.g. admin / '7en8aiDoh!', and other user passwords). These are seeded into the database and stored/compared in plaintext (line 67), exposing credentials.
